title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 170 (Register of directors and key managerial personnel and their shareholding)

content.overview: Section 170 requires every company to keep at its registered office a register containing such particulars of its directors and key managerial personnel as may be prescribed, which shall include the details of securities held by each of them in the company or its holding, subsidiary, subsidiary of its holding company or associate companies. A return containing such particulars is filed with the Registrar on appointment and on any change.
content.glance: Register of directors and KMP at registered office with prescribed particulars including securities held; return filed with ROC on appointment and on change.
content.study: Every company shall keep at its registered office a register containing such particulars of its directors and key managerial personnel as may be prescribed, which shall include the details of securities held by each of them in the company or its holding, subsidiary, subsidiary of its holding company or associate companies. A return containing the particulars of appointment of directors and key managerial personnel and changes among them is filed with the Registrar within the prescribed time. Current-law framing: confirm register at registered office; check prescribed particulars including securities; verify ROC return on appointment/change.

sections.heading: Register
sections.body: Kept at the registered office; contains prescribed particulars of directors and key managerial personnel.

sections.heading: Securities Details
sections.body: Particulars include details of securities held by each director/KMP in the company or its holding, subsidiary, subsidiary of holding, or associate companies.

sections.heading: ROC Return
sections.body: A return of appointment and of changes is filed with the Registrar within the prescribed time.

provisions.title: Register of directors and key managerial personnel and their shareholding

examples.title: Register at registered office
examples.body: A company keeps the register of directors and KMP only at a branch office. Section 170 requires it at the registered office.

examples.title: Change not filed
examples.body: A director is appointed but the company does not file the return of particulars with the Registrar within the prescribed time. Section 170 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Must the register include shareholding in associate companies?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 170 requires particulars to include details of securities held in the company or its holding, subsidiary, subsidiary of its holding company or associate companies.

distinctions.title: Register (s. 170) vs members' right to inspect (s. 171)
distinctions.left: Duty to maintain the register and file returns
distinctions.right: Members' right to inspect the register during business hours and at the AGM

misconceptions.trap: Only directors need be entered; KMP can be omitted.
misconceptions.correction: Section 170 covers both directors and key managerial personnel.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 170 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm register at registered office. II. Check prescribed particulars including securities. III. Verify ROC return on appointment/change. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Register location; particulars; filing status; precise relief.

examTips: Return to ROC on appointment and change.
